newsitem.title: USA: Circus Circus to seek Detroit casino license.
newsitem.headline: Circus Circus to seek Detroit casino license.

text.p: Circus Circus Enterprises Inc, one of the major hotel and casino operators in the United States, on Wednesday said it has joined with a local group to bid on one of three casino licenses in Detroit.
In a statement, Circus said it and the Atwater Group, comprised of over 70 local business, education and civic leaders, have formed a joint venture seeking the license.
In November, Detroit voters approved the building of three casinos to help revitalize downtown. Winners of the licenses are expected to be announced by the end of the year.

Already, MGM Grand Inc has unveiled a partnership to pursue one license and has said it might spend as much as $400 million on a hotel and casino project. Other interested parties include a local group called Greektown Casino LLC and gambling heavyweights Mirage Resorts Inc and Harrah's Entertainment Inc.

In Las Vegas, Circus Circus operates the pyramid-shaped Luxor, medieval-themed castle Excalibur and its flagship Circus Circus-Las Vegas, as well as several other properties. It also operates casinos in Illinois and Mississippi.

"Detroit offers a special opportunity for development of a renowned entertainment center with a casino, which should draw millions of visitors per year," Glenn Schaeffer, Circus' president, said in a statement.
"Circus provides a strong presence in the financial markets, which will ensure the capital to complete a spectacular resort in Detroit on a fast schedule," he added.
Details of their proposal including cost, design and location will be announced at a later date.
